extracted.intended_audience: NIH peer reviewers and applicants (investigators preparing or reviewing RPG/R01/R03/R15/R21/R34 applications)
extracted.subtask_description: Standard definitions and considerations used by NIH study sections to evaluate Research Project Grant (RPG) applications (R01/R03/R15/R21/R34), including overall impact, scored review criteria, and topic-specific review expectations (human subjects, animals, resource sharing, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will provide an overall impact score to reflect their assessment of the likelihood for the project to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved, in consideration of the following review criteria and additional review criteria (as applicable for the project proposed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R01, R03, R21, R34: overall impact = likelihood to exert sustained, powerful influence on the field in consideration of the review criteria and additional review criteria. R15: reviewers will provide an overall impact/priority score to reflect their assessment of the likelihood for the project to make an important scientific contribution, provide research opportunities to students, and strengthen the institution's research environment, in consideration of the review criteria and additional review criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Guidance for R03, R15, R21, and R34 applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Special expectations for small, exploratory, AREA, and clinical trial planning grants that affect how reviewers evaluate applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small Research Grant Program (R03): supports discrete, well-defined projects that can be completed in two years with limited funding. Applications may not contain extensive detail; reviewers should evaluate the conceptual framework and general approach. Appropriate justification may be via literature citations, other-source data, or investigator-generated data. Preliminary data are not required, particularly for pilot/feasibility studies. Academic Research Enhancement Award (R15): objectives are to provide support for meritorious research, strengthen research environments at schools not major NIH recipients, and expose students to research. Preliminary data are not required but may be included. Exploratory/Developmental Research Grant Program (R21): supports novel ideas, new model systems, tools, or technologies with potential for significant impact; need not have extensive background or preliminary information. Reviewers will focus on conceptual framework, level of innovation, and potential to advance understanding. NIH Clinical Trial Planning Grant Program (R34): supports development of Phase III clinical trials (team establishment, data management/oversight tools, recruitment strategy, protocol finalization). Not designed for preliminary data collection or pilot studies to support trial rationale. Reviewers focus evaluation on rationale and design/protocol in its current early form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project address an important problem or a critical barrier to progress in the field? If the aims of the project are achieved, how will scientific knowledge, technical capability, and/or clinical practice be improved? How will successful completion of the aims change the concepts, methods, technologies, treatments, services, or preventative interventions that drive this field?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R01, R03, R21, R34: evaluate importance of problem/barrier, improvements to knowledge/technique/practice, and potential to change field. R15: same questions plus: If funded, will the AREA award substantially strengthen the school/academic component and expose students to research?

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the PD/PIs, collaborators, and other researchers well suited to the project? If Early Stage Investigators or those in the early stages of independent careers, do they have appropriate experience and training? If established, have they demonstrated an ongoing record of accomplishments that have advanced their field(s)? If the project is collaborative or multi-PD/PI, do the investigators have complementary and integrated expertise; are their leadership approach, governance and organizational structure appropriate for the project?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R01, R03, R21, R34: assess qualifications, experience, track record, and suitability for the project; for multi-PD/PI evaluate complementary expertise and leadership/governance. R15: same plus assessment of PDs/PIs' experience supervising students in research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the application challenge and seek to shift current research or clinical practice paradigms by utilizing novel theoretical concepts, approaches or methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether concepts/approaches/methodologies/instrumentation/interventions are novel to one field or novel more broadly, or whether a refinement/improvement/new application of existing concepts is proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the overall strategy, methodology, and analyses well-reasoned and appropriate to accomplish the specific aims of the project? Are potential problems, alternative strategies, and benchmarks for success presented? If the project is in the early stages of development, will the strategy establish feasibility and will particularly risky aspects be managed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R01, R03, R21, R34: evaluate strategy, methodology, analyses, consideration of potential problems/alternatives/benchmarks, and feasibility/management of risky aspects for early-stage work. If the project involves human subjects and/or NIH-defined clinical research, assess plans to address 1) protection of human subjects from research risks, and 2) inclusion (or exclusion) of individuals on the basis of sex/gender, race, ethnicity, and inclusion (or exclusion) of children, justified in terms of scientific goals and research strategy. R15: similar wording; for clinical research emphasize protection and inclusion of minorities and both sexes/genders and children. R15 also asks whether the application provides sufficient evidence that the project can stimulate student interest toward biomedical/behavioral science careers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the scientific environment in which the work will be done contribute to the probability of success? Are the institutional support, equipment and other physical resources available to the investigators adequate for the project proposed? Will the project benefit from unique features of the scientific environment, subject populations, or collaborative arrangements?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R01, R03, R21, R34: assess institutional support, equipment, physical resources, and unique environmental features/collaborations/populations. R15: evaluate institutional support/equipment/physical resources, likely availability of well-qualified students to participate, and evidence that students have in the past or are likely to pursue careers in biomedical/behavioral sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: For research that involves human subjects but does not involve one of the six categories of research that are exempt under 45 CFR Part 46, the committee will evaluate the justification for involvement of human subjects and the proposed protections from research risk relating to their participation according to the following five review criteria: 1) risk to subjects, 2) adequacy of protection against risks, 3) potential benefits to the subjects and others, 4) importance of the knowledge to be gained, and 5) data and safety monitoring for clinical trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For research that involves human subjects and meets the criteria for one or more of the six exemption categories under 45 CFR Part 46, the committee will evaluate: 1) the justification for the exemption, 2) human subjects involvement and characteristics, and 3) sources of materials. See the Guidelines for the Review of Human Subjects for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women, Minorities, and Children
rubrics_metrics.description: When the proposed project involves human subjects and/or NIH-defined clinical research, the committee will evaluate the proposed plans for the inclusion (or exclusion) of individuals on the basis of sex/gender, race, and ethnicity, as well as the inclusion (or exclusion) of children to determine if it is justified in terms of the scientific goals and research strategy proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the Guidelines for the Review of Inclusion in Clinical Research for additional information; reviewers evaluate justification for inclusion/exclusion decisions relative to scientific goals and strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee will evaluate the involvement of live vertebrate animals as part of the scientific assessment according to the following five points: 1) proposed use of the animals, and species, strains, ages, sex, and numbers to be used; 2) justifications for the use of animals and for the appropriateness of the species and numbers proposed; 3) adequacy of veterinary care; 4) procedures for limiting discomfort, distress, pain and injury to that which is unavoidable in the conduct of scientifically sound research including the use of analgesic, anesthetic, and tranquilizing drugs and/or comfortable restraining devices; and 5) methods of euthanasia and reason for selection if not consistent with the AVMA Guidelines on Euthanasia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the Worksheet for Review of the Vertebrate Animal Section for additional information on review of this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess whether materials or procedures proposed are potentially hazardous to research personnel and/or the environment, and if needed, determine whether adequate protection is proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider biosafety, biocontainment, and environmental protection measures; determine adequacy of proposed protections for personnel and environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: For Resubmissions, the committee will evaluate the application as now presented, taking into consideration the responses to comments from the previous scientific review group and changes made to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess adequacy of responses to previous critique and the extent and appropriateness of changes made in the resubmitted application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: For Renewals, the committee will consider the progress made in the last funding period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate productivity, accomplishments, and whether the proposed continuation is justified by prior progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision
rubrics_metrics.description: For Revisions, the committee will consider the appropriateness of the proposed expansion of the scope of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Revision application relates to a specific line of investigation presented in the original application that was not recommended for approval, the committee will consider whether the responses to comments from the previous scientific review group are adequate and whether substantial changes are clearly evident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications from Foreign Organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess whether the project presents special opportunities for furthering research programs through the use of unusual talent, resources, populations, or environmental conditions that exist in other countries and either are not readily available in the United States or augment existing U.S. resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider unique advantages or augmentations provided by foreign settings, populations, or resources, and whether they merit support despite being outside the U.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agent Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess the information provided in this section of the application, including 1) the Select Agent(s) to be used in the proposed research, 2) the registration status of all entities where Select Agent(s) will be used, 3) the procedures that will be used to monitor possession use and transfer of Select Agent(s), and 4) plans for appropriate biosafety, biocontainment, and security of the Select Agent(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess compliance with select agent regulations, registration, monitoring procedures, and adequacy of biosafety/biocontainment/security plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will comment on whether the following Resource Sharing Plans, or the rationale for not sharing the following types of resources, are reasonable: 1) Data Sharing Plan; 2) Sharing Model Organisms; and 3) Genome Wide Association Studies (GWAS)/Genomic Data Sharing Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on reasonableness of plans or provided rationale for not sharing; consider feasibility and potential value of broader data/resource availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will consider whether the budget and the requested period of support are fully justified and reasonable in relation to the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether requested funds and project duration are appropriate for the scope of work; note any discrepancies or unjustified items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Comments to the Applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may provide guidance to the applicant or recommend against resubmission without fundamental revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional narrative advice or recommendations regarding resubmission; may include constructive guidance, suggested revisions, or strong recommendations against resubmission absent major changes.
